newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela foreign reserves rise to $15.117 bln.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela foreign reserves rise to $15.117 bln.

text.p: Venezuela's foreign reserves rose $244 million, or 1.6 percent, to $15.117 billion in the week to Nov 18, according to figures released by the central bank on Friday.
Reserves were up from $14.873 bln on Nov 11, the bank's latest weekly bulletin of indicators showed.
Since the start of the year, reserve levels have risen $5.394 billion, or 55 percent.

The Central Bank had earlier indicated that it would not release reserve figures until Monday due to technical problems but a bank spokesman said an effort had been made to ensure that the figures were released on Friday as usual.
Government officials had targeted foreign reserves to grow by $1.5 billion over the course of 1996 as part of Venezuela's IMF- supported economic adjustment program.
Venezuela's foreign reserves fell $1.784 billion, or 15.5 percent, in 1995 to end the year at $9.723 billion.
